lessons.title: @c_pron
lessons.intro: Often, but not always, nasal vowels occur at the end of a word.

sections.heading: Vowels
sections.body: a : as the 'a' in "about" [uh] · á : as the 'a' in "father" [ah] · â : as the 'a' in "about" [uh] , usually nasalized, as it's typically follows by n or m [uhn] · ã, -am, -an, -âm, -ân : a nasal sound like 'um' in "umbrella" [uhn] · e : like 'i' in "him" [ih] , or nearly absent at the end of many words and in unstressed syllables · é : long sound as the 'e' in "get" [eh] · ê : similar to the 'i' in "ill" [ih] · -em, -en, -êm, -ên : nasal sound like 'en' in "end" [ehn] · i : as the 'ee' in "week" [ee] · -im, -in, -ím, -ín : nasal sound like 'ing' in "wing" [een] · o : as the 'o' in "open" [oh] , often reduced or nearly silent at the end of words after a "t" or "d"; in many positions, like the 'oo' in "boot" [oo] · ó : like the 'a' in "awful" [aw] · ô : like the 'oa' in "coat" [oh] , but less rounded · -om, -on, -ôm, -ôn : nasal sound like "Ohm" [ohn] · u : as the 'oo' "boot" [oo] · -um, -un, -úm, -ún : nasal sound like 'um' in "hum" [oom]

sections.heading: Consonants
sections.body: b : [b] · c : [k] · d : [d] · f : [f] · g : [g] . When followed by "u" the "u" is usually silent when it's followed by "e" or "i". · h : silent at the beginning of a word; see digraphs the "ch", "lh", and "nh" below · j : [zh] · k : [k] · l : [l, ll] · m : [m] · n : [n] · p : [p] · q : [k] . The following "u" is pronounced like the semi-vowel "w" before "a" as in quando ("when", KWUHN-doo, /ˈkwɐ̃.du./) or "o" (uncommon words only). The "u" is silent when followed by an "e" as in quente ("hot", KEHN-t(ih), /ˈkẽ.tɨ/) or an "i" as in quinta ("fifth", "Thursday", "farm", or "villa", KEEN-tuh, /ˈkĩ.tɐ/). · r : [r] , or [rr] , depending on context. "rr" is always guttural. · s : [s] · s : [sh] , e.g., gostaria ("I/he/she would like", goosh-tuh-REE-uh, /guʃ.tɐ.ˈɾi.ɐ/) · s : [z] , e.g., casa /KAH-zuh/ · t : [t] · v : [v] · w : [w] · x : [ks] , [sh] , or [s] , depending on context · y : [y] · z : [z]

sections.heading: Common diphthongs
sections.body: ãe, ãi : as 'ai' in "main" but nasalised [uhny] · ai, ái : like 'ie' in "pie" [igh] · ão : as 'ow' in "cow" but nasalised [uhnw] · au, áu : as 'ow' in "cow" [ahw] · ei, éi, êi : as 'ay' in "play" [ehy] · eu, êu : as in the exclamation "ew!" [ihw] · eu, éu : like "eh oo" [ehw] · õe : as 'oy' in "oyster" but nasalised [ohny] · oi, ôi : as 'oy' in "oyster" [ohy] · oi, ói : as 'oy' in "oyster", but less rounded [awy] · ou : as 'oo' in "took", but less rounded [ohw] · ui : as 'wee' in "week" [ooy] , may nasalised as in the word "mui" [oony]

lessons.title: @c_numbers
lessons.intro: For numbers 1,000,000,000 and above, European Portuguese uses the long scale (Brazilian Portuguese uses the short scale).

sections.heading: @c_remember
sections.body: Portugal uses the 24-hour clock, so 8AM is written as 08:00 or 08h00, noon as 12:00 or 12h00, 8:30PM as 20:30 or 20h30, and midnight as 00:00 or 00h00 (sometimes 24:00 or 24h00). This is what you will find in timetables and business hours. In casual conversation, the Portuguese do use 12-hour time.
